# Signatories and community support

[Shaurita D. Hutchins](https://github.com/sdhutchins) will lead the project in collaboration with [Samuel Bharti](https://github.com/samuelbharti). Both are PhD candidates at the University of Alabama at Birmingham.

**Hutchins will lead educational design and community development.** She will develop the metadata profile, coordinate reference fixtures, and establish accessibility and contribution guidance. She brings experience in Carpentries instruction, reproducible R/Bioconductor workflows, and [browser-based educational modules](https://cfdetrainingcenter.github.io/candidate-genetic-variants/).

**Bharti will lead software architecture and engine integration.** He will harden and extend adapters that use existing engine checks and produce validation reports in a common format. A former Posit intern, he develops Shiny applications, R packages, and automated documentation workflows. His teaching work includes [r-for-beginners](https://github.com/samuelbharti/r-for-beginners), an adaptation of Software Carpentry lessons with accompanying slides.

We will jointly design the package API and registry, and share responsibility for governance and the reference fixtures.

We requested public feedback through [r/Stats](https://www.reddit.com/r/Stats/comments/1wvj3wd/for_people_who_teach_or_learn_r_how_do_you_find/) and the [learnr webR discussion](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/766#issuecomment-5944771998). Community contributor [\@coatless](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/766#issuecomment-5944898742) pointed us to learnr2 and Quarto Live. That feedback helped us focus on shared metadata and checks, though the proposed profile still needs review.

We are seeking additional review from engine maintainers, Carpentries and Bioconductor educators, and university and community instructors.
